name: Union Square (Piața Unirii)
facts: Piața Unirii is famous for its beautiful Baroque architecture and colorful buildings, making it one of the most picturesque places in Timișoara.
It is home to the impressive Roman Catholic Dome, built in the 18th century, and the Serbian Orthodox Cathedral, reflecting the city's multicultural heritage.
The square received its current name in 1919, when Romanian troops entered Timișoara, marking an important moment in the city's history.

name: Victory Square (Piața Victoriei)
attribution: Photo: Marius Catalin Boldeanu — CC BY-SA 4.0
facts: Piața Victoriei was one of the main places where people gathered to protest against the communist regime in December 1989.
At one end of the square stands the Romanian National Opera, while at the other end is the impressive Orthodox Metropolitan Cathedral, built between 1936 and 1940.

name: Liberty Square (Piața Libertății)
attribution: Photo: Marius Catalin Boldeanu — CC BY-SA 4.0
facts: In the 18th century, the square was used by Habsburg troops for military gatherings and parades.
It was also known as Parade Square and Arms Square.
The square received the name Liberty Square for the first time in 1848, during the Hungarian Revolution.
In its center, you can also admire a beautiful Baroque monument dedicated to the Virgin Mary and Saint John of Nepomuk, created in 1756.

name: Maria Theresia Bastion (Bastionul „Maria Theresia”)
facts: Built between 1732 and 1734, it was originally used as a military food storage facility, holding supplies such as flour and salt.
Out of the original nine bastions of the Habsburg fortress, it is the only one that survived almost intact.
Today, it hosts cultural exhibitions, restaurants and events.

name: Metropolitan Cathedral (Catedrala Mitropolitană)
facts: The cathedral was completed in 1940 and has 11 towers, including its central tower, which reaches approximately 83 metres in height.
The area around the cathedral became one of the main gathering points for protesters during the Romanian Revolution against communism in December 1989.

name: Timișoara National Museum of Art (Muzeul Național de Artă din Timișoara)
facts: The museum is housed in the impressive Baroque Palace, originally built in the 18th century and later renovated.
The building is one of the most important architectural landmarks in the city.
The museum features Romanian and European art, including paintings, decorative arts and works by renowned artists such as Corneliu Baba.

name: Trajan Square (Piața Traian)
facts: Piața Traian was designed in the 18th century as the central square of the Fabric neighborhood, an area that developed as an important commercial and industrial center.
The square features beautiful buildings in Baroque and Secession styles, including the Millennium Catholic Church, built in 1896, one of the area's most recognizable landmarks.

name: Millennium Catholic Church (Biserica Millennium)
facts: The church was founded in 1896, when its foundation stone was laid on October 4.
It was consecrated on October 13, 1901.
Designed by architect Lajos Ybl, the church was built in Neo-Romanesque style and features two impressive towers and elaborate decorative elements.

name: Neptune Palace (Palatul Neptun)
facts: Built between 1912 and 1914, the building was initially known as Hungária Fürdő.
It housed a large public bath and an indoor swimming pool, which were important facilities for the local community.
Designed by architect László Székely, the palace is famous for its Hungarian Secession style and its impressive decorative façade.

name: Fabric Synagogue (Sinagoga din Fabric)
facts: The synagogue was designed by architect Lipót Baumhorn and constructed between 1897 and 1899.
Its architecture combines eclectic historicist elements with Neo-Moorish influences.
It served as an important religious and cultural center for the Jewish community in Fabric.

name: Roman's Square (Piața Romanilor)
facts: Piața Romanilor is one of the historic squares of the Fabric district, developing as an important urban space connecting the historic neighborhood with the rest of the city.
The square is home to the Millennium Catholic Church, whose construction began in 1896 and which was consecrated in 1901.
Designed by architect Lajos Ybl, the church is built in Neo-Romanesque style.

name: Saint Mary's Square (Piața Sfânta Maria)
facts: The nearby Reformed Church on Timotei Cipariu Street was the starting point of the protests on December 16, 1989, which marked the beginning of the Romanian Revolution in Timișoara.
In the center of the square stands the statue of the Virgin Mary, inaugurated in 1906.
According to local tradition, it marks the place where Gheorghe Doja, leader of the 1514 peasant uprising, was executed.

name: Water Palace (Palatul Apelor)
facts: Completed in 1901, the building originally served as the headquarters of the Timiș–Bega Water Management Company, which was responsible for managing waterways and water-related works in the region.
Designed by architect Lipót Baumhorn, the palace features Art Nouveau (Secession) elements, including decorative fish, seashells, seahorses and aquatic plants.

name: Iosefin Water Tower (Turnul de apă din Iosefin)
facts: Completed in 1914, the tower was part of Timișoara's water distribution system.
Standing 52 metres tall, it contained two reservoirs: one for drinking water (500 m³) and another for industrial water (250 m³), taken directly from the Bega River.

name: Timișoara North Railway Station (Gara de Nord)
facts: The first railway line connecting Timișoara to the European railway network opened on November 15, 1857.
The current station's original monumental building was inaugurated in 1897 and designed in Neoclassical style by Hungarian architect Ferenc Pfaff.

name: Decebal Bridge (Podul Decebal)
facts: Built between 1908 and 1909, it was considered one of the most impressive reinforced-concrete beam bridges in Europe at the time.
Its elegant Art Nouveau (Secession) design, with its distinctive curved lines and decorative details, makes it an architectural landmark.

name: Mihai Viteazu Bridge (Podul Mihai Viteazu)
attribution: Photo: Mihai mircea moise — CC BY-SA 4.0
facts: A wooden bridge existed at this location before the mid-19th century and appears on an 1853 map of Timișoara under the name Bischofsbrücke (Bishop's Bridge).
The wooden bridge was reinforced in 1898 and replaced by the current reinforced-concrete bridge, which was opened in 1913.
Historically known as the Bishop's Bridge, it is officially named Podul Mitropolit Andrei Șaguna and is popularly known as Podul Mihai Viteazu.

name: Maria Bridge (Podul Maria)
facts: The current Podul Traian, also historically known as Podul Huniade or Podul de la Maria, was designed by architect Elemér Wachtel.
Its construction was initiated in the early 1910s and completed in 1917, replacing an earlier metal bridge.
It became an important crossing over the Bega Canal, connecting the historic Cetate area with Iosefin.

name: Bega River Promenade (Faleza Bega)
facts: The Bega Canal was developed in the 18th century, starting in 1728, to control flooding and facilitate the transportation of goods, including timber.
It later became an important commercial waterway connecting Timișoara to the wider European river network.
Today, the riverbanks offer walking and cycling paths, green spaces and parks.

name: Rose Park (Parcul Rozelor)
facts: The park was inaugurated on July 19, 1891, during the Industrial and Agricultural Exhibition in Timișoara.
By 1934, the park featured approximately 1,400 varieties of roses.
It also includes an open-air theatre, which hosts cultural events and festivals.

name: Botanical Park (Parcul Botanic)
facts: The first design for the park was created in 1966 by architect Silvia Grumeza.
The park began opening to visitors in 1986, with planting and development works continuing through 1990.
It covers approximately 9.8 hectares and contains themed botanical sections representing different geographical regions.

name: Anton von Scudier Central Park (Parcul Central „Anton von Scudier”)
facts: Established in 1880 by order of General Anton von Scudier, the park was created on the site of a former military and civilian cemetery that had been closed in the 18th century.
The park's Aleea Personalităților (Avenue of Personalities) displays 24 bronze busts of important figures from Banat's history, including politicians, writers, musicians and artists.

name: Ion Creangă Children's Park (Parcul Copiilor Ion Creangă)
facts: The park's development began in 1858 under the name Franz Joseph Park, with the initial landscaping completed in 1891.
Throughout history, it was also known as Mihai Eminescu Park and Pioneers' Park.
Following a major modernization project, the park reopened in 2012 with themed playgrounds and recreational areas.
